newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenyan drought-hit coffees attract fair prices.
newsitem.headline: Kenyan drought-hit coffees attract fair prices.

text.p: Lighter, drought-hit coffees received fair prices despite their low quality, coffee auction officials said on Tuesday.
"The drought-affected coffee did get a good price relative to its quality," said one dealer, adding that prices were particularly competitive for the higher grades.
Premium grade ABs averaged $271 per 50 kg from $257 while grade AAs averaged $356 from $326. The Coffee Board of Kenya sold all 20,526 60-Kg bags on offer compared to 20,035 bags sold last week.
